params.body:
Fixes bevinding de-api-update-start-een-registratie-na. Fixes #578. Replaces #754, which failed
static analysis for a reason worth keeping: typing the parameter made `$vehicle?->dealer` a nullsafe
on something that can no longer be null, and the baseline entry that used to ignore it stopped
matching. So the nullsafe is gone and the baseline is one line shorter, 924 to 923.

`VehicleApiService::updateCarpassInit()` took an untyped parameter, and `VehicleApiController::update()`
handed it `$decrypted_id` instead of the vehicle. PHP reads a property on an int as null with no more
than a warning, so `filled($vehicle->chassis_number)` was false and the guard never passed: an API
update carrying a Car-Pass URL started no registration. The create path passes a real vehicle and has
worked the whole time, which is why this survived.

The parameter is typed now. That is the actual repair: the same slip is a TypeError instead of
silence, for this caller and the next one. The caller passes the vehicle, refreshed, because the
guard reads `mileage` and `carpass_id` and those were written a line earlier.

**How far this reaches, measured on production rather than assumed.** `update()` refuses anyone whose
role does not carry `type = 1`. Exactly one role does ("Premium trader"), with one user. All 37 update
calls in the log, 17 to 22 September, came from other roles and were answered
`{"error":"update-method temporary unavailable","status":200}`. So the defect is real and reachable,
but by one partner, and that is worth saying out loud next to a fix.

Two things found while measuring, neither touched here:

- `ApiLogRepository` prunes with `->where('created_at', '<', now()->subDays(14))->orWhere('action',
  'api.update.vehicle')->delete()`. The `orWhere` is not grouped, so every `api.update.vehicle` row is
  deleted on every prune regardless of age. That is why the log holds five days of update calls and
  months of everything else, and it removes exactly the evidence this kind of question needs.
- The update endpoint has answered "temporary unavailable" to twelve dealers' feed ("Doorlinken
  Voorraad") for as long as the log reaches, with HTTP 200. If that is deliberate it is fine; if it
  is not, nobody would have noticed.

The second test pins the guard rather than the symptom: handing an id is refused out loud. Run against
`VehicleApiService` as it stands on main it fails with `Attempt to read property "chassis_number" on int`.
params.title: The API update hands over the car, not its id
